text:
Two teams, two stars who want out, and two very different ways of handling it. Dylan Larkin left the Red Wings on Oct. 29, told them he will no longer play for Detroit, and has been suspended without pay since. Interim GM Shawn Horcoff called it "status quo" this week, per NHL.com, while Elliotte Friedman said Friday that Minnesota's offer, which he believes is Danila Yurov and three first-round picks, has been out there a while. Detroit, without a captain since September, has gone 0-5-0, outscored 18-9, and blew a three-goal lead in Florida on Thursday. The chances say the slide is real: 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those five.

Nikita Kucherov told Tampa he won't re-sign and wants a trade, as the AP reported last month; general manager Julien BriseBois has said he has no intention of trading him. Kucherov's answer has been to play. CBS Sports counts six points in his last two games, and Daily Faceoff noted he keeps giving everything despite the request. The Lightning are 4-1-0 in their last five and have 55% of the five-on-five expected goals this season. Brayden Point is on injured reserve (ESPN estimates Dec. 2), Brandon Hagel has moved onto the top line and scored in three straight (five goals), and Anthony Cirelli is now day-to-day.

Detroit goes with Daniil Tarasov over John Gibson, a reasonable choice given Tarasov's .919 and 6.6 goals saved above expected in eight games. Andrei Vasilevskiy is near even (-0.1). Andrew Copp plays his 800th NHL game, and he's also the man in Larkin's spot, up to 19:48 a night. Viktor Arvidsson and Alex DeBrincat are pointless in five straight despite 4.1 and 4.4 expected points over that stretch; the chances are there, the finish isn't.

Our numbers have Hagel at 42% to score and Kucherov at 82% for a point. Tampa won the first meeting 4-2 on Nov. 3. Playoff odds: Lightning 96%, Red Wings 15%.
headline: Red Wings without Larkin, Lightning with Kucherov's request
